title: British ultrarunner, mom Jasmin Paris first woman to conquer hellacious Barkley Marathons
claims: Jasmin Paris finished the 2024 Barkley Marathons in 59 hours, 58 minutes and 21 seconds, with 99 seconds to spare of the 60-hour cut-off.
The race spans approximately 160 kilometres and features about 60,000 feet of elevation gain and descent, roughly twice the height of Everest.
Since the race was extended to its current 100-mile distance in 1989, only 20 people have completed it within the 60-hour timeframe.
There are no aid stations along the course, save for two locations offering water.
The race was conceived by Gary Cantrell and Karl Henn in 1986.
The race was inspired by the escape of James Earl Ray, who covered approximately 12 miles over 54 hours after escaping from a nearby prison in 1977.
The course is altered each year but typically consists of five loops of around 20 miles each.
Only 35 participants are granted entry each year.
Entry requires a 1.60 US dollar fee and an essay explaining why the applicant should be allowed to run; successful applicants receive a letter of condolence.
The race starts at any time between midnight and noon on the race day, and the blowing of a conch shell signals the final hour before the start.
There are no course markings; competitors must commit the route to memory before the race.
Mark Williams became the first runner to complete the race within the 60-hour limit, in 1995.
Brett Maune holds the fastest finish, 52 hours, 3 minutes and 8 seconds, set in 2012.
Paris reached the fourth lap in both 2022 and 2023, the first woman to do so since 2001.
